To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

the stress system in the peripheral tissues, especially skin, is an integral part of the stress response, and that NGF-dependent pathways are involved in stress-induced neuroinflammatory skin disorders.

(1) NGF is released from the skin in a CRF-dependent manner in response to stress; (2) NGF induces the expression of CRF in skin mast cells, which in turn release CRF and SP; and (3) SP is released from skin sensory nerve endings, leading to a vicious circle of mast cell activation.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the neuroendocrine control of skin mast cells.
the role of the brain in the pathophysiology of inflammatory skin conditions, with the goal of developing new treatments.
the neuroendocrine mechanisms underlying stress-induced and -aggravated skin disorders.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
stress can precipitate or aggravate skin disorders.

the stress-induced skin diseases are not a result of stress, but a result of a stress-induced neuroinflammatory response, which is a result of stress-induced activation of mast cells and the NGF-dependent neuroinflammatory pathway.
stress is an important risk factor for the development of atopic dermatitis, although the underlying mechanisms are still not fully understood.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the skin is a target of stress-induced neuroinflammation.
stress induces skin disorders, and that this effect can be explained in part by the release of nerve growth factor (NGG) and the subsequent activation of mast cells.
stress is a major factor in the development of skin diseases.
The main takeaway from our work is that

stress-induced or -aggra- vated skin disorders may involve a complex interaction between stress- induced activation of sensory nerves and mast cells in the skin, leading to increased release of inflammatory mediators, including NGF, and to the development or aggravation of skin disorders.
